Scripts in /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/verify/refute_screen_cut/ (read-only w.r.t. the repos):

r1_reporters_panel.py — rebuilds the reporter's exemplar panel verbatim (their seed 13, D=400, S=800). Their numbers reproduce bit-for-bit: floor cells 65.57%, median 11 distinct values/day; z>0.3 screens 26.81% at hl=0 but 20.00% at hl=5 and hl=20; (sign=-1, hl=0) screens 0.00%, `sm` is bit-identical to `ctx.base` (np.array_equal == True), train diff +0.000000 and valid diff +0.000000.

r3_gate_passing_fixed.py — the decisive test. Derived the cliff algebraically from `_zrank` (a tie block of size k above `a` smaller names is screened iff a + (k-1)/2 > 0.8(n-1); with the block at the top, a = n-k, so screened iff k < 0.4n + 0.6) and confirmed it. On panels with a floor block of k of n names and the rest continuous, distinct_fraction = (n-k+1)/n, so every floor fraction up to 50% clears the >= 0.5 gate:
  floor 20% dist 0.80 PASS -> inverted direction screens 20.00%
  floor 30% dist 0.70 PASS -> 30.00%
  floor 35% dist 0.65 PASS -> 35.00%
  floor 40% dist 0.60 PASS -> 40.00%   (double the stated depth)
  floor 41% dist 0.59 PASS ->  0.00%   (the no-op)
  floor 50% dist 0.50 PASS ->  0.00%
On a gate-passing floor=41% panel with the candidate independent of the label, all five genuine cells are negative on train (-1.22 to -1.82) and the 0%-screen cell wins: reward() returns score 0.0 exactly (`r["score"] == 0.0` is True, train 0.0, valid 0.0), fit = 0.03*0.0 = 0.0, finite. Over 20 independent gate-passing panels, 13 of 20 report score EXACTLY 0.0; their honest scores would have been median -2.1553 (range -3.1152..-0.8821), i.e. fit clamped from -0.0647 to 0.0, and all 13 tie at the top of a negative archive. AlphaCube admits them: src/alphacube/mining/gp.py:461 rejects only non-finite fitness.

r4_depth_confound_and_coverage.py — on a gate-passing floor=35% panel (dist 0.6512) where the floor block genuinely underperforms, (sign=-1, hl=0) screens 35.00% and scores +3.8449; the same cell forced to a constant 20% depth scores +0.9287. Coverage: candidate NaN on 10%/20%/40% of names screens 20.00% of the names that have a candidate value but 18.00%/16.00%/12.00% of the base universe.

r6_hl_flip_scan.py — 24 gate-passing floor panels (22%–38%), implemented grid vs the same grid at a constant 20% depth. hl=0 wins 23/24 as implemented because it is the deepest cell; the (hl, sign) argmax FLIPS in 10 of 24 once depth is held constant. Reported score minus constant-depth score: median +1.317, max +3.621. The THR=0.2 verdict flips in at least two scanned cases (+0.042 implemented vs +0.364 constant-depth; +1.239 vs -0.442).

r5_fix_adequacy.py — tests the suggested fix. candidate = exp(known/50) (distinct_fraction 1.0000, gate PASSES): at sign=-1 it screens a legal 20.00% of names but 0.00% of the base's long-book holdings, so train and valid diffs are exactly +0.000000 and reward() returns score 0.0. Also confirmed `best = None` + `_, sign, hl, sm, tr = best` raises "TypeError: cannot unpack non-iterable NoneType object". And top-20%-by-count over the candidate's finite cells removes 16.00% / 12.00% of the base universe at 20% / 40% candidate NaN — identical to the z-cut.

Lattice bound (inline check): I1's day_ops are occupancy ratios on a 241-minute day, so values sit on a k/241 lattice. At S=5000 names the maximum attainable distinct_fraction is ~0.048 for a bare day_op and for `cross_max(day_*, w)` (max of a lattice stays on the lattice) — both always gated out — versus ~0.54 for `cross_mean(day_*, 15)` and ~0.72 for `cross_mean(day_*, 30)`.
result.corrected_fix:
The defect is real; the suggested fix is directionally right but incomplete in four ways, and one part of it would make things worse.

1. A depth band cannot catch the no-op, because a 0% screen is not the only way to score exactly 0.000. r5 shows a candidate that screens a perfectly legal 20.00% of names and still returns exactly +0.000/+0.000, because the screened set overlaps 0.00% of the names the base's long book actually holds (sign=-1 on a candidate monotone in the base pushes the base's own bottom fifth down, leaving the top decile untouched). A `[0.10, 0.30]` band admits that cell. This route needs no saturating panel at all and is not filtered upstream, because idea_search.py:330 exempts long_screen from the rho_pool/rho_known gate, so base-correlated candidates are exactly what this reward collects. The quantity to guard is the realised change to the BOOK, not the screened fraction: reject a (sign, hl) whose screened set intersects none of the base's held names — or, simplest and strictly stronger, reject a cell whose `sm` is unchanged from `ctx.base` on the held names. Record both the realised screened fraction and that holdings overlap in the reward dict.

2. The rejection branch must be an explicit outcome, not a `continue`. steer.py:418 initialises `best = None` and steer.py:440 unpacks `_, sign, hl, sm, tr = best`; if every cell is rejected, that raises TypeError (reproduced). The reward must return `score: float("-inf")` with the kind/sign/hl fields filled, which idea_search.py:154 already maps to fit = -inf.

3. Do not take "the top ceil(0.2*n) by rank with an explicit deterministic tie rule" as the primary cut. A stable-argsort tie-break inside a straddling block selects by column index, i.e. by symbol order — precisely what dg.distinct_fraction's own docstring (diagnose.py:136-139) warns against. It buys reproducibility, not meaning: a saturating candidate would then *look* like a clean 20% screen while its membership is arbitrary, which is worse than today's visible 0%/40% cliff. The reporter's parenthetical alternative — push the whole straddling block out and record it — is the honest one, but it contradicts "20% by construction"; the two cannot both hold. Correct behaviour: cut by count, record the realised depth, and reject the cell when either the realised depth leaves the band or the straddling tie block is large enough that the cut inside it is arbitrary (e.g. block size > some small fraction of n).

4. Cutting by count does not fix the coverage rescaling, contrary to the implication that the fraction becomes 20% "by construction". Verified in r5: top-20%-by-count over the candidate's finite cells still removes 16.00% of the base universe at 20% candidate NaN and 12.00% at 40%, identical to the z-cut. To hold the depth at 20% of what the base ranks, the count must be `k = ceil(0.2 * #isfinite(base_t))` drawn from `isfinite(base_t) & isfinite(z_t)`, and a cell whose candidate coverage cannot reach that k must be rejected rather than silently scored at a shallower depth — otherwise the reward keeps preferring high-coverage candidates for a reason unrelated to the hypothesis.

Also worth fixing while in this code: the argmax key is the screened book's absolute train Sharpe (steer.py:439), which makes a no-op's key exactly `base_tr`. Keying on `r["long_sharpe"] - base_tr` is equivalent for ranking but makes the no-op's zero explicit and easy to reject.
result.reasoning:
VERDICT: not refuted. I reproduced every component of the finding, including on panels that clear the gate I hoped would kill it.

What reproduces exactly (r1): the reporter's own panel gives 26.81% screened at hl=0 vs 20.00% at hl=5/20, and (sign=-1, hl=0) screens 0.00% with `sm` bit-identical to `ctx.base`, so both period differences are exactly 0.000000. The exactness is structural, not numerical luck: steer.py:435 is `np.where(isfinite(base), np.where(isfinite(z) & (z>0.3), ..., base), nan)`, so with an empty mask `sm` IS `base` cell for cell and `book_row` returns the same floats, making `s_tr = s_va = 0.0` identically.

My best refutation attempt, and why it failed: scripts/idea_search.py:144-148 gates on `dg.distinct_fraction(panel) >= 0.5` and sets fit = -inf BEFORE steer_reward is called, and `reward()` with long_screen has exactly one caller (idea_search.py:151 — grep over the repo confirms; the only other import is tests/test_steer.py). The reporter's exemplar panel has distinct_fraction 0.013750, so it FAILS that gate and never reaches the reward. Their failure scenario asserts "distinct_fraction is not the binding gate here", and for the panel they actually submitted as evidence that assertion is false. That is the one factual error in the report.

But the gate does not protect the reward, which is what decides the verdict. A floor block of k out of n names with the rest continuous has distinct_fraction = (n-k+1)/n, so floor fractions up to 50% clear >= 0.5 — and the cliff I derived from `_zrank` (whole block screened iff k < 0.4n + 0.6) sits at 40%, entirely inside the passing region. Confirmed numerically (r3): floor 30% PASS -> inverted direction screens 30.00%; floor 40% PASS -> 40.00%, double the documented "top fifth"; floor 41% PASS -> 0.00%. So the broken behaviour needs only a 20%+ modal block, which is a much milder requirement than the reporter's 65%.

The number-changing consequences, all on gate-passing panels:
- Score inflation and half-life confound (r4, r6): against the same grid held at a constant 20% depth, the reported score is inflated by a median of +1.317 Sharpe (max +3.621), and the reported (hl, sign) argmax flips in 10 of 24 panels — hl=0 wins 23/24 as implemented purely because the raw panel's ties make it the deepest cell. So `p_hl`, `p_sign` and `p_score` in episodes/*/evidence.json do not mean what they say, and the THR=0.2 pass/fail verdict flips in at least two of the 24 scanned cases (+0.042 vs +0.364, and +1.239 vs -0.442). That is the headline gate of the steer-vs-control protocol.
- The exact-zero no-op (r3): on a gate-passing floor=41% panel with the candidate independent of the label, every genuine screen dilutes the base's long book and is negative on train, so the only non-negative cell is the one that does nothing — and it wins. 13 of 20 independent panels report score EXACTLY 0.0 instead of a median honest -2.1553. This is not an exotic corner: "the candidate is a bad screen" is the common case, and it is precisely the condition that hands the argmax to the no-op. fit = 0.0 is finite, so gp.py:461 admits it; with cull_clusters' `cutoff = best - 0.5*abs(best)` (clustering.py:102) a best of 0.0 collapses the survivor band to `fitness[i] > 0.0`, which nothing satisfies — the link to the companion finding holds.
- Coverage (r4): 10%/20%/40% of names NaN in the candidate screens 18.00%/16.00%/12.00% of the base universe. Exactly as claimed; the reporter's 16.76% is their panel's version of my 16.00%.

Severity: I agree with medium, and would argue the depth/half-life confound (which fires at any modal block over 20%) is the larger half, not the 0.000 no-op the title leads with.

One link I could not verify, stated for the record: whether idea I1's real panels carry a 20%+ modal block. No real data is reachable from this machine. What I could bound is which shapes reach the reward at all — on a ~5000-name panel the maximum attainable distinct_fraction is ~0.048 for a bare occupancy ratio and for `cross_max(day_*, w)` (the max of a 241-point lattice stays on that lattice), so both are always gated out, including I1's own seed #1 `cross_max(day_zero_ratio(Ret), 15)`; only `cross_mean(day_*, 15/30)` (~0.54/~0.72) and `cross_ema` can pass. So in a real I1 run this defect fires through the cross_mean/cross_ema-wrapped occupancy ratios, whose floor block is "a name never flat on any of the w days" — plausibly large for day_at_max_ratio / day_at_min_ratio, whose minimum (1/241, a unique intraday extreme) is the modal value for liquid names, but I verified the fraction only synthetically. This caveat bounds the blast radius; it does not rescue the reward, since the defect is in the cut itself and fires at a 20% modal block.
